TWO FINDS, AND ONE OF THEM EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE OF RULE 50

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE McGILL DAILY, VOL. 78 NO. 83, MONDAY 20 FEBRUARY 1989 (Special Issue)
   A Kamp Kanawana counsellor recruitment advertisement, p. 14
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Identifier: McGillLibrary-mcgill-daily-v78-n083-february-20-1989-13147
Found by the whole-corpus sweep of 9,890 McGill student publication items (p_479).
"Kanawana" occurs twice in the issue, both in this advertisement — once in the
display headline, which the OCR renders "KANflWANA".

  "Kamp Kanawana, a COED camp for children AGED 7-15, is situated in the heart
  of the Laurentians near St. Sauver [sic], on 1200 ACRES OF LAND AND THREE
  PRIVATE LAKES. We offer the youth of Montreal a summer filled with the
  excitement of discovery and personal growth. If you're interested in a summer
  that will allow you to share your enthusiasm, creativity and leadership with
  children, phone or write to: Kamp Kanawana, 1441 Drummond St., Montreal
  (Quebec) H3G 1W3, (514) 849-8331.
  THE EXPERIENCE THAT LASTS A LIFETIME!"

THREE THINGS, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES SOMETHING.

(a) THE FORTY-ONE-YEAR RECRUITING SERIES NOW HAS A THIRD POINT. The same corpus
    gave the camp's counsellor advertisements of 20 May 1948 and 25 May 1949,
    over R. D. Locke's name. This is the same practice — the camp buying display
    space in a university paper to fill its staff — still running in 1989. The
    1948-49 ads gave a phone number of "MA. 8331"; this one gives 849-8331. THE
    LAST FOUR DIGITS ARE THE SAME AND THIS IS NOT ASSERTED AS CONTINUITY. Under
    the old letter-exchange system MA maps to 62, which would give 628-8331, not
    849-8331; and 849 is the exchange of the Y's Metropolitan Offices at 1441
    Drummond Street, which the bulletin of 29 January 1970 gives as 849-5331. So
    either the subscriber number survived a change of exchange, or 8331 recurs
    by chance. It is written down as a coincidence worth someone checking, not
    as a fact.

(b) 1200 ACRES AND THREE PRIVATE LAKES, IN 1989, IN THE CAMP'S OWN WORDS.
    wiki/site/the-kanawana-site.md tabulates the reported acreage and gives
    "1,200 acres 'of private land and lakes'" on the authority of The Gazette of
    18 April 1974, noting that the figure "is not a journalistic outlier — it is
    the tail of a period." This extends that period by fifteen years and removes
    the journalist: the camp itself was still advertising 1200 acres in 1989.

(c) "THE EXPERIENCE THAT LASTS A LIFETIME" IS OLDER THAN THE FILM THAT BEARS THE
    NAME. This wiki knows the phrase as the title of a 1993 YMCA promotional
    documentary, *Kamp Kanawana: The Experience that Lasts a Lifetime*, produced
    by Laurentien Productions — cited that way in history/centennial-1994.md and
    traditions/myths-and-legends.md — and as the title of Grace McMorris's
    MA thesis (Concordia, 2023), which borrowed it. [The year was written 2019
    in this cache's first draft and corrected against the wiki's own citation
    within the hour -- a date carried from memory rather than read.] Nothing in this project says it was a slogan
    before it was a title. IT WAS. It closes this advertisement in February 1989,
    four years before the film, set as a tagline. The documentary took its name
    from the camp's own advertising line rather than giving one to it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. "REPORT OF THE MONTREAL YMCA CAMP PERROT FOR BOYS AND GIRLS", 1948
   Health and Safety section — a Kanawana staff doctor turning up at Perrot
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Identifier: 1948-report-of-the-montreal-ymca-camp-perrot-for-boys-and-girls

HOW THIS WAS FOUND, WHICH IS THE POINT. The main sweep had already recorded this
item and read it. The item carries TWO `_djvu.txt` files and the sweep read only
the first, per the bug recorded as rule 50 (f_5427). `rescan_multi.py`, written
to back-fill exactly that, searched the second file and hit on it — within its
first 224 items. This passage would otherwise have stayed unread behind a CLEAN.

  "HEALTH AND SAFETY. The general health of the camp was good. However, a great
  many cases of poison ivy were treated from contacts made outside the camp
  property. An educational campaign was constantly mentioned to help the campers
  recognize this obnoxious weed when on hikes. The greatly improved hospital
  facilities were extensively used and all the campers, counsellors and staff
  members were urged to have their cuts, scratches, ailments, attended to at
  once before deeper infections were allowed to get a hold.

  DR. KELSO OF ST. ANNE'S again gave unstintingly of his skill and professional
  services. His ready response to all our calls was a source of great aid to us
  in maintaining the camp health and safety. When Dr. Kelso left on his holidays
  he asked the doctor taking over his practice to keep a watchful eye on his
  wards. DR. LOUGHEED, HIS SUCCESSOR, CONTINUED THE INTEREST IN OUR CAMP AND WE
  WERE AGREEABLY SURPRISED TO LEARN THAT DR. LOUGHEED HAD FORMERLY BEEN ON THE
  STAFF OF KAMP KANAWANA."

(The OCR of this typescript is poor — "holideys", "obioxious", "teKing OVer" —
and is silently regularised above; nothing of substance is in doubt.)

WHAT IT GIVES. Two named camp doctors, neither of whom occurs anywhere else in
this project: greped across wiki/, kb/facts.json, project-docs/ and
sources/sources.json before this was written, "Kelso" 0 and "Lougheed" 0. Dr.
Kelso of Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue attended Camp Perrot on Île Perrot, unpaid
("gave unstintingly"), across more than one season ("again"). And DR. LOUGHEED
HAD BEEN ON KANAWANA'S OWN STAFF at some earlier date, which is a named medical
member of Kanawana staff — a category this project has almost nothing in. The
report gives no year for that service and no first names.

It also documents the mechanism by which a country doctor's summer camp duty
passed to his locum, and the "greatly improved hospital facilities" at Perrot,
which sits beside the John W. Ross Memorial Hospital material already in
wiki/site/camp-perrot.md.

NULL RESULTS. "Kanawana" occurs once in the report, here. Neither doctor's first
name is given anywhere in it.
